rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse turns from obstinate rejecters to people approaching Islam and removes the apparent conflict with the command to fight after the sacred months: they must be allowed to hear the proof.
rows.anchor: شروع في بيان حكم المتصدين لمبادىء التوبة من سماع كلام الله تعالى

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: In the conditional construction, the noun is raised by an implicit verb explained by the overt verb; treating it as an initial subject is mistaken because إن governs verbs, not nouns.
rows.anchor: ومن زعم ذلك فقد أخطأ كما قال الزجاج لأن إن لكونها تعمل العمل المختص بالفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: استجارك means that a polytheist seeks security and protection after the appointed period has ended; فأجره means grant him safety.
rows.anchor: أي استأمنك وطلب مجاورتك بعد انقضاء الأجل المضروب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hearing entails reflection and learning the truth of the call; mentioning hearing alone suffices because the Arabs addressed are eloquent, and the speech is evidence for divine oneness and God's transcendence above likeness.
rows.anchor: ويتدبره ويطلع على حقيقة ما تدعوا إليه والاقتصار على ذكر سماع لعدم الحاجة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase كلام الله is variously explained as the verses establishing oneness, Sūrat Barāʾa, or the whole Qurʾān, which contains the complete proofs.
rows.anchor: وقيل : سورة براءة وقيل : جميع القرآن لان تمام الدلائل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He takes حتى as causal, attached to the command to grant protection; the context and the following instruction to escort the listener home support this over a merely terminal sense.
rows.anchor: و ( حتى ) للتعليل متعلقة بما عندها وليست الآية من التنازع

rows.speaker: الفاضل ابن العادل
rows.claim: Most grammarians reject treating the two verbs as competing governors here: making استجارك govern would require حتى to govern a pronoun, which they allow only under poetic necessity.
rows.anchor: على ما صرح به الفاضل ابن العادل حيث قال : ولا يجوز ذلك عند الجمهور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An approacher's need in the reported exchange concerns religion, but the report does not establish that all worldly needs are excluded; the wording may be general.
rows.anchor: فالمراد بما فيه من الحاجة هي الحاجة المتعلقة بالدين لا ما يعمها

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: A polytheist asked whether someone from their group could come to Muhammad after the truce period to hear God's speech or meet a need without being killed; ʿAlī answered no and cited the protection verse.
rows.anchor: وما روي عن علي كرم الله تعالى وجهه أنه أتاه رجل من المشركين

rows.speaker: شيخ الإسلام
rows.claim: He reasons that attaching the grant of protection to hearing God's speech also ties the request for protection to that purpose or to a comparable religious need.
rows.anchor: قال شيخ الإسلام ان تعليق الاجارة بسماع كلام الله تعالى يستلزم تعلق الاستجارة

rows.speaker: سري الدين المصري
rows.claim: He objects that taking حتى as a mere endpoint is ruled out by the command to escort the person to safety after he has listened.
rows.anchor: قال المولى سري الدين المصري : إن جعلها للغاية يأباه قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Maʾman is the place where the person is safe, especially his people's territory; construing it as a place noun is preferable to taking it as a verbal noun with an omitted modifier.
rows.anchor: أي مسكنه الذي يأمن فيه أو موضع أمنه وهو ديار قومه على أن المأمن إسم مكان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse does not disprove the Muʿtazilite doctrine of inner speech: hearing can be attributed to the sign that conveys speech, and كلام can denote inner or voiced speech by shared or figurative usage.
rows.anchor: ولا حجة في الآية للمعتزلة على نفي الكلام النفسي لأن السماع قد ينسب إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are people ignorant of Islam and the reality of the message; granting safety lets them understand and removes any remaining excuse.
rows.anchor: ما الاسلام وما حقيقة ما تدعوهم إليه أو قوم جهلة فلا بد من إعطاء الأمان

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: He holds that the protection ruling remains operative; al-Ālūsī judges this the stronger position.
rows.anchor: والآية كما قال الحسن محكمة

rows.speaker: سعيد بن أبي عروبة
rows.claim: A report transmitted by Abū al-Shaykh says the verse was abrogated by the command to fight all polytheists; the same view is also attributed to al-Suddī and al-Ḍaḥḥāk.
rows.anchor: وأخرج أبو الشيخ عن سعيد بن أبي عروبة أنها منسوخة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The respite is variously set at four months, said by al-Nīsābūrī to be the sound Shāfiʿī position, or left to the ruler's judgment, which al-Ālūsī considers more apt.
rows.anchor: فقيل : أربعة أشهر وذكر النيسابوري أنه الصحيح من مذهب الشافعي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The questions challenge the polytheists to acknowledge God's exclusive right to divinity. Provision comes from heavenly causes such as rain and sun and earthly materials; the earth receives what the sky provides.
rows.anchor: احتجاجا على حقية التوحيد وبطلان ماهم عليه من الإشراك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For من السماء والأرض, من may mark origin; alternatives take it as explanatory after an ellipsis or partitive after an implied إضافة, meaning provisions from the inhabitants of heaven and earth.
rows.anchor: فمن على هذا لإبتداء الغاية وقيل : هي لبيان ( من ) على تقدير المضاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disconnected أم introduces a transition, not a correction, and asks who creates and forms hearing and sight, protects them from injury, or controls their persistence and loss; الملك is figurative in these readings.
rows.anchor: ( أم ) منقطعة بمعنى بل والإضطراب إنتقالي لا إبطالي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The reading of ملك السمع والأبصار as creating them best matches the sequence pairing creative power with provision, as in the cited question about any creator who provides.
rows.anchor: وقيل : والمعنى الأول أوفق لنظم الخالقية مع الرازقية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The living brought from the dead can mean an animal from a drop and a drop from an animal, or bringing life from death and death from life; interpreting the pair as believer and unbeliever is also reported, while the first explanation is preferred.
rows.anchor: ومن الناس من فسر الحي والميت هنا بالمؤمن والكافر والأول أولى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Managing the affair generalizes beyond the specific visible matters just listed and signals that all affairs originate with God and return to Him, although humans cannot know their full details.
rows.anchor: وهو تعميم بعد تخصيص ما اندرج تحته من الأمور الظاهرة بالذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The polytheists answer Allah without hesitation because the evidence is too plain for denial; الله is the subject with an omitted predicate meaning that God alone performs these acts.
rows.anchor: لا مجال للمكابرة والعناد في شيء من ذلك لغاية وضوحه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse does not explicitly call God one of the inhabitants of heaven and earth; although texts say He is in heaven in a manner befitting Him, there is no need to change من from its origin sense.
rows.anchor: لم يرد صريحا كونه تعالى من أهل السماء والأرض وأن ورد كونه جل وعلا في السماء

rows.speaker: صاحب الإنتصاف
rows.claim: He reads the verse as refuting the Qadariyyah claim that God provides only lawful sustenance while people provide themselves with forbidden sustenance, exposing that claim as hidden associationism.
rows.anchor: هذه الآية كافحة لوجوه القدرية الزاعمين أن الأرزاق منقسة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some mystics claim the cosmic pole manages the world and holds up the sky; they may answer that it acts by God's permission, and use المدبرات أمرا for a non-divine manager.
rows.anchor: يزعمون أن الذي يدبر الأمر في كل عصر قطبه وهو عماد السماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some argue that the pole and God differ only in consideration because the pole has attained perfect nearness; critics say this collapses into unity of being, which most theologians and some Sufis, including al-Imām al-Rabbānī, reject.
rows.anchor: فالقول بأن القطب هو المدبر كالقول بأن الله سبحانه هو المدبر بلافرق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The proposed analogy between a pole and the angels or Jesus managing by God's permission fails: the question asks for the ultimate source to which management returns, so the polytheists can only answer God.
rows.anchor: وأجيب بأن السؤال إنما هو عمن ينتهي إليه الأمر فلا يتسنى لهم إلا الجواب المذكور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In أفلا تتقون, the interrogative rebukes the actual failure to fear, with the connective following an implied premise: you know this, yet do not fear; the omitted object is God's punishment.
rows.anchor: أي أتعلمون ذلك فلا تتقون والخلاف في مثل هذا التركيب شهير

rows.speaker: القاضي
rows.claim: Al-Qāḍī's analysis appears to make تتقون govern two objects, but al-Ālūsī rejects that implication: here it governs one, with the object omitted.
rows.anchor: وكلام القاضي يوهم أنه متعد إلى مفعولين وليس بذاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: فذلكم summarizes the qualities the questioners acknowledged; the grammar may make Allah an adjective and ربكم the predicate, or treat Allah as predicate and ربكم as apposition, while الحق qualifies or further predicates lordship.
rows.anchor: فذلكة تقرر والإشارة إلى المتصف بالصفات السابقة حسبما إعترفوا به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the true Lord, there is only error: abandoning worship of God alone necessarily leads to worship of another, and worship that associates others with Him is not accepted.
rows.anchor: فمن تخطى الحق وهو عبادة الله تعالى وحده لا بد وإن يقع في الضلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One construal takes الحق as worship of God and الضلال as worship of others; another takes الحق as the true Lord and الضلال as idols, with an expanded view covering monotheism and other worship generally.
rows.anchor: وقيل : المراد بالخحق والضلال مايعم التوحيد

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: Asked about the testimony of habitual chess and backgammon players, Mālik says he doubts their testimony's worth and applies the verse's judgment that all beyond truth is error.
rows.anchor: ويؤيده ماأخرجه ابن أبي حاتم عن أشهب قال : سئل مالك عن شهادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The interrogative in فأنى تصرفون expresses astonishment and denial of their actual turning away; its force exceeds simply denying the act's occurrence.
rows.anchor: فكيف تصرفون عن الحق إلى الضلال والإستفهام إنكاري بمعنى إنكار الواقع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The rebuke truly targets the cause of their turning, since on the author's doctrine God is the agent of the act and it would be incoherent to express astonishment at God's own act.
rows.anchor: ولعل ذلك الإنكار والتعجب متوجهان في الحقيقة إلى منشأ الصرف وإلا

rows.speaker: المعتزلة
rows.claim: The Muʿtazila say the polytheists themselves create and perform their turning from truth; the agent is left unspoken because the act is too shameful to attribute openly to them.
rows.anchor: وذهب المعتزلة أن فاعل الصرف نفسه المشركون فهم الذين صرفوا أنفسهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The condemned people lose themselves by exchanging worship of God for worship of idols.
rows.anchor: بإشتراء عبادة الآلهة بعبادة الله تعالى شأنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is that they exchanged guidance for error and the afterlife for this world, losing the worldly enjoyment and authority obtained by that exchange.
rows.anchor: وقيل : ( خسروا ) بسبب تبديلهم الهداية بالضلالة والآخرة بالدنيا

rows.speaker: البحر
rows.claim: Al-Baḥr supplies an omitted modifier: they lost the happiness and comfort of their souls, since the selves themselves remain tormented.
rows.anchor: وفي البحر أنه على حذف مضاف أي ( خسروا ) سعادة أنفسهم وراحتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He prefers the literal wording: their continuing existence in torment is effectively their being kept in loss.
rows.anchor: وتعقب بأن إبقاءه على ظاهره أولى لأن البقاء في العذاب كالإبقاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What they had invented, their supposed gods and their intercession, has vanished from them.
rows.anchor: ضل عنهم ما كانوا يفترون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are the greatest losers in degree or amount; the definite predicate marks exclusivity, and taking هم as a separator or subject further emphasizes that judgment.
rows.anchor: أي لا أحد أبين أو أكثر حسرانا منهم فأفعل للزيادة إما في الكم أو الكيف

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj analyzes لا as negating an omitted clause such as their deed benefiting them and جرم as a past verb meaning earned; the following أن-clause states what the deed earned.
rows.anchor: عن الزجاج أن لا نافية ومنفيها محذوف أي لا ينفعهم فعلهم مثلا و جرم فعل ماض

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: An unnamed poet uses جرمت to mean earned or committed, as evidence for the verbal reading of جرم.
rows.anchor: وقال الشاعر : نصبنا رأسه في جذع نخل بما ( جرمت ) يداه

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sībawayh takes لا as negative and جرم as the verb حقّ, with the following clause as its subject: their deed cannot benefit them, since their loss is certain.
rows.anchor: ونقل عن سيبويه أن لا نافية حسبما نقل عن الزجاج و جرم فعل ماضي بمعنى حق

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān says Sībawayh and al-Khalīl treat the combined لا جرم as meaning certainly; the following clause is its subject.
rows.anchor: وذكر أبو حيان أن مذهب سيبويه وكذا الخليل أيضا كون مجموع ( لا جرم ) بمعنى حق

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: Al-Kisāʾī analyzes لا as negative and جرم as its indeclinable noun, with an omitted predicate and a preposition omitted before أن; the idiom means no opposition or prevention.
rows.anchor: وعن الكسائي أن ( لا ) نافية ( وجرم ) إسمها مبني معها على الفتح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view makes جرم a noun meaning cutting off: their being the greatest losers will never cease, so no contrary state interrupts it.
rows.anchor: وقيل : إن ( جرم ) إسم ( لا ) ومعناه القطع من جرمت الشيء أي قطعته

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Sīrāfī transmits from al-Zajjāj that لا جرم first meant not to admit someone into sin, then conventionally came to mean inevitably; al-Farrāʾ is also credited with this explanation.
rows.anchor: ونقل السيرافي عن الزجاج أن ( لا جرم ) في الأصل بمعنى لا يدخلنكم في الجرم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other analyses derive the idiom from جرم as falsehood or earning, yielding the sense truly or certainly; lexicographers record variant forms, some of whose attribution as eloquent Arabic is doubted.
rows.anchor: وفي البحر أن ( جرم ) عليه إسم ( لا ) وقيل : إن ( جرم ) بمعنى باطل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After completing the account of the disbelievers' conduct and fate, the discourse turns to believers and their good outcome, completing the contrast with the preceding praise of believers.
rows.anchor: ثم إنه تعالى لما ذكر طريق الكفار وأعمالهم وبين مصيرهم وما لهم شرع في شرح حال أضدادهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Intervening particles between لا and جرم are generally treated as extra; the author tentatively explains a reported form without لا as saying that the fact needs no further assertion.
rows.anchor: وحكي بغير لا جرم أنك أنت فعلت ذاك

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: ʿAshāʾ is the interval from sunset prayer until night prayer; العشاآن names the two evening prayers.
rows.anchor: كما قال الراغب من صلاة المغرب إلى العتمة والعشاآن : المغرب

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan is said to have read عَشِيًّا as a diminutive; another reading عَشِيّ has a shortened form and is variously analyzed as a plural or as an original form altered by sound change.
rows.anchor: وعن الحسن أنه قرأ عشيا بضم العين وفتح الشين وتشديد الياء منونا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alternative construals of the nonstandard readings face objections: the proposed حذف of tāʾ and plural pattern are not licensed, so another vocalic-shift and elision account is offered.
rows.anchor: وأورد عليهما بأنه لا جواز لمثل هذا الحذف وأنه لا يجمع أفعل فعلاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A proposed reading takes the word as a plural of عشوة, a venture in darkness or confusion, emphasizing the brothers' deceit; another takes it as a flame, emphasizing their haste and glee.
rows.anchor: وقيل : هو جمع عشوة مثلث العين وهي ركوب أمر على غير بصيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ordinary reading means evening; they may have returned then because they could not reach home sooner or because darkness made their excuse easier to stage.
rows.anchor: والظاهر الأول وإنما جاءوا عشاء إما لأنها لا يصلوا من مكانهم إلا في ذلك الوقت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some take this as the evening of the same day, while others infer a later evening from a report that Joseph stayed in the well three days and Judah brought him food.
rows.anchor: ظاهر كلان بعضهم الأول وذهب بعضهم إلى الثاني بناءا على ما روي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their weeping was feigned: they displayed tears without genuine grief, as liars commonly imitate sorrow.
rows.anchor: أي متباكين أي مظهرين البكاء بتكلف لأنه لم يكن عن حزن

rows.speaker: الشعبي
rows.claim: Al-Shaʿbī recounts a woman crying before the judge Shurayḥ; when people pointed to her tears, Shurayḥ recalled that Joseph's brothers came to their father crying.
rows.anchor: أخرج ابن المنذر عن الشعبي قال : جاءت إمرأة إلى شريح تخاصم

rows.speaker: الأعمش
rows.claim: Al-Aʿmash quips that after Joseph's brothers, even one's father should not be believed.
rows.anchor: وقال الأعمش : لا يصدق أباك بعد إخوة يوسف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In a report, Jacob asks whether some wage has afflicted them; when they say no, he asks what happened to them and where Joseph is.
rows.anchor: وفي بعض الآثار أن يعقوب عليه السلام لما سمع بكاءهم قال : ما بالكم أجري

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddī explains their contest as racing on foot.
rows.anchor: على ما روي عن السدي

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjāj takes their contest to be archery; the author favors this because ʿAbd Allāh's reading says ننتضل, meaning to shoot arrows against one another.
rows.anchor: كما قال الزجاج أو في أعمال نتوزعها من سقي ورعي واحتطاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other proposed contests involve dividing tasks such as watering, herding, and gathering wood, or hunting.
rows.anchor: أو في أعمال نتوزعها من سقي ورعي واحتطاب أو في الصيد وأخذه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The objection that running is childish and useless is answered: it can train them to run in battle or to fend off a wolf; نستبق can mean نتسابق, and the derived forms can share the same sense.
rows.anchor: وثمرته التدريب في العدو لمحاربة العدو ومدافعة الذئب مثلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their claim that Joseph was left by the belongings presents him as safe among clothes and provisions, within sight and only briefly unattended, so they deny negligence in guarding him.
rows.anchor: بل تركناه في مأمنا ومجمعا بمرأى منا وما فارقناه إلا ساعة يسيرة

rows.speaker: شيخ الإسلام
rows.claim: He explains that the brothers' mention of the belongings shows they left Joseph in a safe place where threats were unlikely.
rows.anchor: فكان ما كان قاله شيخ الإسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He reads them as literally claiming that a wolf ate Joseph; the proposal that they hinted the wolf ate the belongings is an unwarranted departure from the plain sense.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أنهم لم يريدوا إلا أن الذئب أكل يوسف ولم يقصدوا بذلك تعريضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They mean Jacob would not trust their account even if he regarded them as honest and reliable because of his strong love for Joseph; reading ولو كنا as an admission they were truthful would make them admit lying by contrast.
rows.anchor: أي موصوفين بالصدق والثقة لفرط محبتك فكيف وأنت سيء الظن بنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: دم كذب means blood characterized by falsehood, as though it were falsehood itself; the source also allows the passive sense blood falsely alleged to be Joseph's.
rows.anchor: أي ذي كذب أو وصف بالمصدر مبالغة كأنه نفس الكذب وعينه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zayd ibn ʿAlī's accusative كذبا is parsed as a circumstantial accusative from the brothers, meaning they came lying; it may instead qualify the blood or be causal, though a circumstantial from an indefinite noun is disfavored.
rows.anchor: وقرأ زيد بن علي رضي الله تعالى عنهما كذبا بالنصب وخرج على أنه في موضع الحال

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: ʿĀʾisha and al-Ḥasan are reported to read كَدِب with dāl; it is a separate lexical form meaning muddy, fresh, or dry, and can therefore express opposite senses.
rows.anchor: وقرأت عائشة رضي الله تعالى عنها والحسن كدب بالدال المهملة وليس من قلب الذال

rows.speaker: صاحب اللوامح
rows.claim: The source of al-Lawāmiʿ explains the dāl form as having a trace or mark, like the white spots that appear in young men's nails.
rows.anchor: وقال صاحب اللوامح : المعنى ذي كدب أي أثر لأن الكدب بياض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some grammarians treat the blood as a vivid simile for a false mark on the shirt, without an omitted possessive modifier.
rows.anchor: ولم يعتبر بعض المحققين تقدير المضاف وجعل ذلك من التشبيه البليغ أو الإستعارة

rows.speaker: أبو البقاء
rows.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ takes على قميصه as a circumstantial phrase modifying the blood; grammarians dispute whether a circumstantial can precede a genitive governed by a preposition.
rows.anchor: وقوله سبحانه : ( على قميصه ) على ما ذهب إليه أبو البقاء حال من دم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the preferred construal, the brothers came with false blood placed above Joseph's shirt; other grammatical accounts make them arrive possessing the shirt, with the blood as a circumstance, but the difference is minor.
rows.anchor: والمعنى أتوا بدم كذب فوق قميصه ولا يخفى إستقامته

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and Mujāhid report that the brothers slaughtered a lamb and smeared its blood on Joseph's shirt.
rows.anchor: لطخوا بدمها القميص كما روي عن ابن عباس ومجاهد

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda's report says they instead killed a gazelle and smeared its blood on the shirt; Jacob found no tooth or claw marks and called the wolf unusually merciful.
rows.anchor: وأخرج ابن أبي حاتم وأبو الشيخ عن قتادة أنهم أخذوا ظبيا فذبحوه فلطخوا بدمه القميص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Further reports describe Jacob kissing the shirt and weeping until his face was stained, or collapsing unconscious; Judah checked for breath, lamented that they had lost their brother and father, and Jacob revived near dawn.
rows.anchor: وفي رواية أنه أخذ القميص وألقاه على وجهه وبكى حتى خضب وجهه بدم القميص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: سولت لكم means that their selves made an evil deed seem attractive and easy; al-Rāghib defines it as painting what one desires in the mind as beautiful.
rows.anchor: وقال الراغب : هو تزيين النفس لما تحرص عليه وتصوير القبيح بصورة الحسن

rows.speaker: الأزهري
rows.claim: Al-Azharī derives تسويل from the person's desire or wish, which beautifies falsehood to the one pursuing it; a less likely derivation links it to laxity of the nerves.
rows.anchor: وقال الأزهري : كأن التسويل تفعيل من سوال الإنسان وهو أمنيته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob knew the story was false because Joseph's shirt was intact; the shirt is also linked to his restored sight and to Joseph's innocence when it was torn from behind.
rows.anchor: وعلمه عليه السلام بكذبهم قيل : حصل من سلامة القميص عن التمزيق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is that Jacob exposed their inconsistencies: after asking why a wolf left the shirt intact, one brother blamed robbers, prompting Jacob to ask why robbers would leave the shirt they needed more than the killing.
rows.anchor: وقيل : من تناقضهم فإنه يروى أنه عليه السلام لما قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even knowing they lied, Jacob grieved because he feared Joseph's suffering, or because separation from loved ones is unbearable; the author allows both fear and separation as causes.
rows.anchor: ولعله مع هذا العلم إنما حزن عليه السلام لما خشي عليه من المكروه

rows.speaker: قطرب
rows.claim: One ellipsis supplies my affair or my patience as the subject of فصبر جميل.
rows.anchor: أي فأمري صبر جميل أو فصبري صبر جميل كما قال قطرب

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: Al-Khalīl supplies a verbal sense: what I will do is that; other analyses understand the phrase as an omitted subject and predicate.
rows.anchor: أو فالذي أفعله ذلك كما قال الخليل

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ construes the phrase as an omitted nominal clause meaning it is beautiful patience.
rows.anchor: أو فهو صبر الخ كما قال الفراء

rows.speaker: أبي
rows.claim: Ubayy, al-Ashhab, and ʿĪsā ibn ʿUmar, as well as a copy attributed to Anas, read both words in the accusative, parsed as an imperative to be patient.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبي والأشهب وعيسى بن عمر فصبرا جميلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The accusative reading is challenged because the form usually requires an imperative; one reply has Jacob address himself: O soul, be patient with beautiful patience.
rows.anchor: وتعقب بأنه لا يحسن النصب في مثل ذلك إلا مع الأمر

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: A Prophetic report attributed to al-Ḥasan defines beautiful patience as patience without complaint to people; the later appeal to God is not excluded.
rows.anchor: والصبر الجميل على ما روى الحسن عنه صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم ما لا شكوى فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says Jacob's brows fell over his eyes and he raised them with a bandage; asked why, he cited time and grief, then God asked whether he was complaining to anyone but Him, and Jacob sought forgiveness.
rows.anchor: وقيل : إنه عليه السلام سقط حاجباه على عينيه فكان برفعهما بعصابة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is the one from whom Jacob continually seeks help; he asks God to expose their lie by preserving Joseph and restoring their reunion, parallel to his later hope that God will bring them all back.
rows.anchor: ومعنى استعانته عليه السلام بالله تعالى على كذبهم طلبه منه سبحانه إظهار كونه كذبا

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: During the slander incident, ʿĀʾisha said her accusers would not believe an oath or accept an excuse and compared herself to Jacob's sons, then invoked God's help; revelation declared her innocence.
rows.anchor: وفي بعض الآثار أن عائشة رضي الله تعالى عنها قالت يوم الإفك : والله لئن حلفت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading asks God to help Jacob bear the claim that Joseph is dead, or to bear the strain of resisting grief; the two clauses parallel worship and reliance in the opening of al-Fātiḥa.
rows.anchor: فقوله : ( فصبر جميل ) يجري مجرى ( إياك نعبد )

rows.speaker: الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Rāzī objects that patiently accepting oppression is not obligatory: Jacob should have investigated, rescued Joseph if alive, or sought retribution if murdered, especially since revelation and his standing suggested Joseph survived.
rows.anchor: للإمام الرازي عليه الرحمة في هذا المقام بحث وهو : أن الصبر على قضاء الله تعالى واجب

rows.speaker: الرازي
rows.claim: The reported replies are that God forbade investigation to intensify the trial; the sons could have prevented it or harmed Jacob; Jacob knew God would protect and exalt Joseph; he wished not to disgrace his sons; or the harm could not yet be undone.
rows.anchor: ثم قال : والجواب أن نقول : لا جواب عن ذلك إلا أن يقال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The parental dilemma is illustrated by a poet: punishing one son for harming another wounds the father, while pardoning or striking both also causes pain.
rows.anchor: ونظير ذلك ما أشار إليه الشاعر بقوله : قومي هم قتلوا أميم أخي فإذا رميت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The interpretation that Jacob promised to conceal his displeasure and keep a cheerful face among his sons is very far from the apparent meaning.
rows.anchor: أنى أتجعل لكم في صبري فلا أعاشركم على كآبة الوجه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gave people some of what they asked for, in keeping with His will, wisdom, and benefit; من is partitive in this reading.
rows.anchor: أي أعطاكم بعض جميع ماسألتموه حسبما تقتضيه مشيئته التابعة للحكمة والمصلحة

rows.speaker: بعض الكاملين
rows.claim: Some scholars take كل to intensify abundance rather than assert exhaustive coverage, as in the cited wording about every door being opened to them.
rows.anchor: وقال بعض الكاملين : إن ( كل ) للتكثير والتفخيم لا للإحاطة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Partitive من does not make كل redundant: both the range of kinds and all members within each kind matter, while human need concerns a kind of thing rather than each individual instance.
rows.anchor: فالمعنى أعطاكم من جميع أفراد كل صنف سألتموه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: سألتموه includes what people need by their condition, whether expressly requested or not; need counts as a request in the language of circumstance, as in the primordial covenant exchange.
rows.anchor: وفسر ( ماسألتموه ) بما من شأنه أن يسأل لاحتياج الناس اليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another account restores an omitted phrase, and God gave you what you asked and what you did not ask, the latter understood from the retained wording.
rows.anchor: وقيل : الاصل وآتاكم من كل ماسألتموه وما لم تسألوه فحذف الثاني

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān objects that if ما is a relative pronoun and its pronoun refers back to it, the proposed antecedent construction would require two same-rank pronouns together or an impermissibly omitted attached pronoun.
rows.anchor: ومنع أبو حيان جواز أن يكون راجعا اليه تعالى ويكون العائد على الموصول محذوفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Others allow those pronoun analyses, arguing that the ban on two same-rank pronouns applies when both appear, and that omitting a detached pronoun is permissible when omission serves a grammatical rather than emphatic purpose.
rows.anchor: وذهب بعضهم إلى جواز كلا التقديرين مدعيا أن منع اتصال المتحدين رتبة خاص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ما may also be a relative, a descriptive noun, or a verbal noun, in the last case meaning what was requested; the pronoun is then understood as referring to God.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن تكون موصوفة والكلام في الضمير كما تقدم وأن تكون مصدرية

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A group including Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Ḍaḥḥāk, al-Ḥasan, Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī, Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, Qatāda, Yaʿqūb, and Nāfiʿ read من كلٍ with tanwīn: God gave each kind of what they needed and asked by their condition.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس والضحاك والحسن ومحمد بن علي وجعفر بن محمد وعمرو بن قائد

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: On that reading, ما can be negative, with من كلٍ as the second object: He gave from everything without their asking; the report is attributed to al-Ḍaḥḥāk.
rows.anchor: وجوز على هذه القراءة أن تكون ( ما ) نافية والمفعول الثاني ( من كل )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He prefers the reading that harmonizes with the uninflected first reading, since it conveys provision of what they asked and therefore, all the more, unasked blessings.
rows.anchor: ولا يخفى أن الوجه هو الأول لما أن القراءة على هذا الوجه تخالف القراءة الأولى

rows.speaker: الواحدي
rows.claim: Al-Wāḥidī says نعمة here is a singular noun used for the verbal noun of bestowing a favor, so it is not pluralized.
rows.anchor: وقال الواحدي : إن ( نعمة ) هنا اسم أقيم مقام المصدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He instead takes نعمة as a collective singular meaning the thing bestowed, with plural reference: if you count God's favors, you cannot number them.
rows.anchor: والمعول عليه ما أشرنا اليه من أنها اسم جنس بمعنى المنعم به والمراد بها الجمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although some say the singular becomes exhaustive through إضافة, the author says the conditional construction itself permits the collective scope intended here.
rows.anchor: وقد نص بعضهم على أن المفرد يفيد الاستغراق بالاضافة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إحصاء fundamentally means counting with pebbles, as Arabs did; it later generalized to counting, with al-Aʿshā's verse using حصى as evidence for pebble-counting.
rows.anchor: وأصل الإحصاء العد بالحصى فان العرب كانوا يعتمدونه في العد

rows.speaker: الأعشى
rows.claim: Al-Aʿshā's line says he is not the most numerous among them in pebbles, since honor belongs to the more numerous group; حصى witnesses the old pebble-counting sense.
rows.anchor: قال الاعشى : ولست بالأكثر منهم حصى وإنما العزة للكاثر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some interpret إحْصاء as bounding or containing all the blessings, to avoid the apparent conflict between counting them and being unable to number them.
rows.anchor: وأول الاحصاء بالحصر لئلا يتنافى الشرط والجزاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One scholar explains the origin of pebble-counting: when a counter completed a bundle of numbers, he set down a pebble to mark it, suggesting that the blessings cannot even be counted to a meaningful stage.
rows.anchor: وقال بعض الافاضل : ان اصله ان الحاسب اذا بلغ عقدا معينا من عقود الاعداد وضع حصاة

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Rāghib and others favor the older pebble-counting interpretation over the alternative account of a counter marking groups with stones.
rows.anchor: وهو من الحسن بمكان الا انه ذهب إلى الاول الراغب وغيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another scholar says that even if one begins counting the details of a single divine blessing, one cannot finish counting it.
rows.anchor: وقال بعض الفضلاء : ان المعنى ان تشرعوا في عد افراد نعمة من نعمه تعالى لاتطيقوا عدها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conditional particle إن is used although failure to count is certain, because people may imagine counting is possible; even one blessing's details cannot be enumerated.
rows.anchor: وإنما أتي بإن وعدم العد مقطوع به نظرا إلى توهم أنه يطاق

rows.speaker: الإمام
rows.claim: The first of the Imam's examples shows that nerve branches, vessels, organs, spirit, celestial bodies, and natural life have so many interdependent functions that human minds grasp only a little of their wisdom.
rows.anchor: وقد ذكر الامام مثالين يستوضح بهما الوقوف على أن نعم الله تعالى لاتحصى

rows.speaker: الإمام
rows.claim: His second example traces one bite of bread to seasons, rain, winds, celestial motions, mined iron and tools, then to the body's complex ability to benefit from food and the medical knowledge needed to understand its effects.
rows.anchor: الثاني أنه اذا اخذت لقمة من الخبز لتضعها في فمك فانظر إلى ماقبلها

rows.speaker: أبو السعود
rows.claim: Abū al-Suʿūd says humans are contingent and deserve neither existence nor its perfections; without continual divine care they would lapse into nonbeing and ruin.
rows.anchor: وقال مولانا أبو السعود قدس سره بعد كلام : وإن رمت العثور على حقيقة الحق

rows.speaker: أبو السعود
rows.claim: Existence must be bestowed at every passing instant as much as at its beginning: continued existence is not self-sustaining, since permanence belongs properly to necessary existence.
rows.anchor: وقال مولانا أبو السعود قدس سره بعد كلام : وإن رمت العثور على حقيقة الحق والوقوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humans are intensely unjust to favors by neglecting gratitude or misusing them, and unjust to themselves by exposing themselves to deprivation through ingratitude; كفار means deeply ungrateful.
rows.anchor: يظلم النعمة باغفال شكرها بالكلية أو بوضعه في غير موضعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conditions sustaining existence include actual causes and conditions, which are finite, and the nonexistence of possible impediments, which may be innumerable at every instant.
rows.anchor: الأمور العدمية التي لها دخل في وجوده ليست كذلك اذ لا استحالة في أن يكون لشيء واحد موانع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since every condition required for a blessing is itself a blessing, and existence and its perfections recur without end through imagined time, blessings are infinite in themselves, not merely beyond human counting.
rows.anchor: وتحقق مايتوقف عليه وجود النعمة نعمة فتحققه سبحانه في كل آن من تلك الآنات نعمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every possible affliction God wards off is also an uncountable blessing; the unending increase in the punishment of the people of Hell illustrates the unbounded possible grades of affliction.
rows.anchor: ما من انسان الا وقد دفع الله تعالى عنه من البلايا ما لا يحيط به نطاق الحصر

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd says God could punish Hell's inhabitants more severely than He does, if He willed.
rows.anchor: وفي رواية ابن أبي الدنيا والبيهقي عن ابن مسعود قال : إن لله تعالى على أهل النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here نعمة has its lexical sense of whatever is agreeable, rather than the technical religious sense of an agreeable outcome praised in the end; that broader meaning allows the examples of removed impediments and enabling conditions.
rows.anchor: المراد بالنعمة معناها اللغوي أعني الأمر الملائم لا المعنى الشرعي

rows.speaker: أبو الدرداء
rows.claim: Abū al-Dardāʾ says someone who recognizes God's favor only in food and drink has little knowledge and is near punishment.
rows.anchor: قال أبو الدرداء رضي الله تعالى عنه : من لم يعرف نعمة الله تعالى عليه الا في مطعمه

rows.speaker: سليمان التيمي
rows.claim: Sulaymān al-Taymī says God gives favors according to His own measure but asks servants for thanks according to their limited capacity.
rows.anchor: وأخرج البيهقي في الشعب وغيره عن سليمان التيمي قال : إن الله تعالى أنعم على العباد

rows.speaker: طلق بن حبيب
rows.claim: Ṭalq ibn Ḥabīb says God's rights are too weighty to fulfill and His favors too numerous to count, so servants should begin and end their days repenting.
rows.anchor: وعن طلق بن حبيب قال : إن حق الله تعالى أثقل من أن يقوم به العباد

rows.speaker: سفيان بن عيينة
rows.claim: Sufyān ibn ʿUyayna says God's greatest favor is teaching servants that there is no deity but God.
rows.anchor: وأفضل نعمه جل شأنه على عباده على ما روى عن سفيان بن عيينة أن عرفهم أن لا إله إلا الله

rows.speaker: داود
rows.claim: In a report from Abū Ayyūb al-Qurashī, David asks for the least of God's favors; God tells him to breathe, and David recognizes breath as that least favor.
rows.anchor: عن أبي أيوب القرشي مولى بني هاشم أن داود عليه السلام قال : رب اخبرني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Existence is commonly called the first pleasure-bearing favor and the source of every perfection; many would sacrifice all worldly property to avoid nonexistence when facing death.
rows.anchor: واشتهر أن اول النعم المقصودة لذتها الوجود وأنه معدن كل كمال

rows.speaker: أبو علي الشبلي
rows.claim: A poem attributed to Abū ʿAlī al-Shiblī or Ibn Sīnā despairs of being born into a life of pain and asks why existence should be celebrated; al-Ālūsī says it denies God's favor and wrongs that favor.
rows.anchor: ومن العجيب ان أبا علي الشبلي البغدادي وقيل : ابن سيناء لم يعد وجود الانسان نعمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second explanation says a person is unjust in hardship by complaining and panicking, but ungrateful in ease by hoarding and withholding.
rows.anchor: وقيل : ظلوم في الشدة يشكو ويجزع كفار في النعمة يجمع ويمنع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first reading better connects the verse to the preceding discussion; الإنسان is generic, exemplified by people who exchange God's favor for disbelief.
rows.anchor: والاول أنسب بما قبله وأل في الانسان للجنس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause is best read as a new explanatory statement answering why people fail to honor favors; reading it as the reason favors are infinite is rejected as unconvincing.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن الجملة استئناف بياني وقع جوابا لسؤال مقدر

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān explains the different ending in al-Naḥl: after describing the favor and associating partners with God, this passage closes with condemnation, whereas al-Naḥl's extended account of favors closes with forgiveness and mercy to invite repentance.
rows.anchor: وفرق أبو حيان بين الختمين بأنه هنا لما تقدم

rows.speaker: عبدالرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم
rows.claim: Al-Sakhāwī transmits Ibn Zayd's claim that this verse was abrogated by the al-Naḥl verse; al-Ālūsī says this view deserves no attention.
rows.anchor: وما نقل السخاوي عن عبدالرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم من أن هذه الآية منسوخة بآية النحل مما لايلتفت اليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative says al-Naḥl closes with forgiveness and mercy because its detailed account of favors and explicit call to gratitude makes failure to thank especially foreseeable; the expanded list of favors is fittingly matched by mercy.
rows.anchor: وقيل : انما ختم سبحانه آية النحل بما ختم للاطناب هناك في ذكر النعم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the mystical allusion, the revealed Book brings people from multiplicity to unity, from the qualities of embodied nature to primordial nature, or from veils of acts and attributes to the pure light of the divine essence.
rows.anchor: فقيل : من ظلمات الكثرة إلى نور الوحدة أو من ظلمات صفات النشأة

rows.speaker: جعفر
rows.claim: Jaʿfar interprets the darknesses as disbelief, innovation, and the self, and the light as faith, the Sunna, and the heart.
rows.anchor: وقال جعفر : من ظلمات الكفر إلى نور الايمان ومن ظلمات البدعة إلى نور السنة

rows.speaker: أبو بكر بن طاهر
rows.claim: Abū Bakr ibn Ṭāhir reads the movement as from the darkness of conjecture to the light of reality.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو بكر بن طاهر : من ظلمات الظن إلى نور الحقيقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's permission means enabling the movement by giving readiness and preparing the causes that bring latent capacity into action.
rows.anchor: ( باذن ربهم ) بتيسيره بهبة الاستعداد وتهيئة أسباب الخروج إلى الفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Mighty is glossed as the One who overpowers darkness with light; the Praiseworthy as perfect in Himself or as giving prepared servants virtues, knowledge, enduring existence, and similar gifts.
rows.anchor: الذي يقهر الظلمة بالنور ( الحميد ) بكمال ذاته أو بما يهب لعباده المستعدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbelievers are veiled from God, and their severe punishment is deprivation; they prefer sensory and formal life to intellectual and spiritual life, obstruct seekers, and seek crookedness in God's straight path.
rows.anchor: المحجوبين ( من عذاب شديد ) وهو عذاب الحرمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Messengers speak in their people's language, using discourse fitted to their state, capacity, and understanding so the message can truly be clear.
rows.anchor: أي بكلام يناسب حالهم واستعدادهم وقدر عقولهم والالم يفهموا فلا يحصل البيان

rows.speaker: عمر
rows.claim: A saying attributed to ʿUmar urges speaking to people in terms they understand, lest they call God and His Messenger liars.
rows.anchor: وعن عمر رضي الله تعالى عنه كلموا الناس بما يفهمون أتريدون أن يكذب الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prophets and saints have specialized language for people versed in knowledge of God; Sufis should not address laypeople in this jargon, just as one should not speak Arabic to a Persian speaker.
rows.anchor: لكل نبي وصديق اصطلاح في كلام المعرفة وطريق المحبة يخاطب به من يعرفه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Many readers of Sufi texts go astray because they do not know the terminology; the author warns that ignorant readers may fall into explicit disbelief and notes a sultanic prohibition on Ibn ʿArabī's books and those of his followers.
rows.anchor: ومنشأ ضلال كثير من الناس الناظرين في كتب القوم جهلهم باصطلاحاتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God misleads those whose readiness has been lost through entrenched dark dispositions and false beliefs, and guides those whose readiness remains or whose false beliefs have not become fixed.
rows.anchor: اضلاله لزوال استعداده بالهيئات الظلمانية ورسوخها والاعتقادات الباطلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mystical reading of God's days is the days of His union with His servants, when He lifted the veils of lordship in a holy presence, drew them near, and bestowed the delight of His address.
rows.anchor: وذكرهم بأيام الله ) وهي أيام وصاله سبحانه حين كشف لعباده
